description:

Google Developer Groups – KSR College of Engineering (GDG KSRCE)

Hack With GDG S4 has been postponed

title: Lean In Hacks 8.0
description:
Lean In Hacks is an 
annual flagship hackathon of Lean In IGDTUW
 - the first chapter of Lean In India. Lean In Hacks is a 
beginner-friendly hackathon
 and has a place for everyone wanting to learn, build, share, and grow in their lives through their unique ideas. Our hackathon journey started in 2020 when we conducted the first edition of Lean In Hacks to give grounds to new thoughts and tools to animate the imaginative and critical thinking side of developers. This time, 
hackers from any college
 can participate in our hackathon, which will be held in 
hybrid mode
. The only requirement is to have 
at least 1 female in your team
! Hackers will be given the 
weekend to build their product online
 and the 
top teams will be given a chance to pitch in the offline mode
. As a beginner-friendly hackathon, we offer a dedicated 
Beginner’s Track
 exclusively for first-time hackers. This track is designed as an 
ideathon
 for 
first-year students
, aimed at fostering innovative thinking, creativity, and confidence in problem-solving. Lean In Hacks is an

title: haxfinity
description:
12–13 December 2026

10:30 AM, 12 December – 10:30 AM, 13 December

Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala Prizes:Exciting prizes — details to be announced

Team size:2–4 participants

Participation: Free Build real solutions, solve meaningful problems, and create something that works. HAXFINITY is a 24-hour hackathon conducted as part of XTHRON ’26, the annual IT fest of the Department of Computer Science, Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur. Students from different colleges and backgrounds will identify problems, build software prototypes, and present their work to judges. The event includes the opening ceremony, a 21-hour project-building window, demonstrations, judging, and awards. There is no compulsory theme. Teams may choose any problem and build a software solution using any suitable technology. Build a product, tool, or prototype that solves a real problem or explores an idea. Build an application using machine learning, generative AI, NLP, computer vision, data analysis, or another AI-related technology. Build technology that improves people’s lives — for example, in education, healthcare, accessibility, sustainability, financial inclusion, or community welfare. Detailed judging criteria will be published before the event. Building window:*11:00 AM, 12 December – 8:00 AM, 13 December (21 hours). Students from all colleges, streams, and experience levels are welcome. You can participate as a beginner, developer, designer, or creative problem-solver. Interests in AI, cybersecurity, web, mobile, cloud, or social-impact technology are all welcome. Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous)

Santhigramam, Eranhimangad

Nilambur, Malappuram, Kerala — 679329 Check-in and travel details will be shared with registered participants. Opportunity to demo projects to judges

Competition Rules All project-specific development must happen during the official building window. Teams may arrive with an idea, but pre-built projects cannot be submitted. Open-source libraries, APIs, datasets, and templates are allowed, subject to their licences. Teams must disclose pre-existing components and AI tools used. Generative AI and AI-assisted development tools are allowed across all tracks. Teams should submit early; late submissions may not be accepted. A working prototype or meaningful demonstration is expected. Teams must be able to explain their technology, process, third-party components, and contributions. Projects must not violate copyright, privacy, security, or applicable law. Organisers may disqualify entries for plagiarism, misconduct, unsafe content, or rule violations. All participants are expected to maintain a respectful, inclusive, and welcoming environment. Participants can approach the organising team for assistance or to report a concern. title: CODERAVE 2.0
description:
CODE • COLLABORATE • INNOVATE - The SLIET Annual  Hackathon. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club

Venue:
 Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab

Mode:
 Hybrid — Online (All India) + Offline (SLIET Campus) Coderave 2.0 is a national-level hybrid hackathon designed to bring together innovative minds, passionate developers, designers, and problem-solvers to transform ideas into impactful technology solutions. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club, this edition offers students an opportunity to demonstrate their creativity, technical expertise, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities through a competitive, time-bound development experience. The hackathon welcomes teams from colleges and universities across India through its online participation track, while SLIET students can participate in the offline campus track. Shortlisted teams will present their ideas through PPT pitches, followed by an intensive 24-hour open-source development challenge in which participants will build, test, and demonstrate their solutions. Whether you are interested in web development, app development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, or other emerging technologies, Coderave 2.0 is your platform to innovate, collaborate, and compete. Round 1 — Registration and PPT Submission:
 The Team Leader registers the complete team and submits the project proposal PPT. Round 2 — PPT Evaluation and Shortlisting:
 Judges evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and presentation quality. Round 3 — PPT Pitch:
 Shortlisted online teams(Max 20 team) pitch through an online meeting. Shortlisted SLIET teams pitch offline on campus on 13 February. Round 4 — 24-Hour Open-Source Hackathon:
 Selected teams(Both online and offline track) build their solutions within the official development window. Round 5 — Final Submission and Evaluation:
 Teams submit their working solution, source code repository, demo video, and other required deliverables. Judges evaluate the final projects and announce the winners. The hackathon is an opportunity to turn ideas into functional prototypes within 24 hours. Teams are expected to develop their solutions during the official event window and use open-source tools, libraries, and technologies wherever possible. Participants must maintain a project repository, provide clear documentation, and ensure that their work is demonstrable. Teams must disclose third-party components and follow applicable open-source licences. Previously developed work must be declared, and the core solution must comply with the organizers' originality requirements. Exciting prizes, goodies, certificates, and recognition await outstanding teams. Final awards, prize amounts, sponsor benefits, and certificate eligibility will be announced through the official event communication. Note:
 The dates above are 
tentative
 until officially confirmed. The year, registration deadline, online pitch schedule, and final evaluation schedule will be published by the organizers. Bring your idea, build your team, and turn innovation into impact. Register for Coderave 2.0 and take your first step toward creating something extraordinary. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club
